metadata.description: Living organisms that make their own food using sunlight, water and air.
The main parts of a flowering plant and what each part does for the plant.
The part of the plant that grows under the ground; it holds the plant in place and absorbs water and minerals from the soil.
The part that holds the plant up and carries water from the root to the leaves and food from the leaves to the rest of the plant.
The usually green, flat part of the plant where food is made using sunlight, water and air.
The part of the plant responsible for reproduction; it can turn into a fruit after pollination.
The part that grows from the flower and protects the seeds inside it.
The part inside the fruit that can grow into a new plant.

metadata.justification: Parts of a Plant is a narrower concept contained within the broader topic of Plants.
The root is one of the main parts of a plant.
The stem is one of the main parts of a plant.
The leaf is one of the main parts of a plant.
The flower is one of the main parts of a plant.
The fruit is one of the main parts of a plant.
The seed is one of the main parts of a plant.
Understanding how the root absorbs water is needed to understand how the stem carries that water upward.
Understanding how the stem carries water is needed to understand how the leaf gets the water it uses to make food.
The fruit grows from the flower, so the flower must be understood first.
Seeds are found inside the fruit, so the fruit must be understood first.

metadata.source_context: Demo curriculum for the interactive-questions prototype: a primary science textbook, Plants unit, lesson 'Parts of a Plant'.
